translationRepairs: Shiji rose to governor of Zhaoyun, and Shiyong became transport commissioner;
Shiji rose to director-general of grain transport, and Shiyong became transport commissioner;

Wikisource transmits 世濟官至遭運總督; 遭運 is not a place name and is the standard graphic garble of 漕運總督 (director-general of grain transport). The original invents a nonexistent Zhaoyun governorship; the proposed office title is accurate.
Shiji rose to governor of Zhaoyun; Shiyong became transport commissioner;
Shiji rose to director-general of grain transport; Shiyong became transport commissioner;
Same as the idiomatic line: Wikisource has 遭運總督, a corrupt form of 漕運總督, not a Zhaoyun governorship. The proposed literal office title correctly restores grain-transport administration.
Nine attendants including Ma Yungiao, Tang Jinbao, and Zhu Zhaoyuan died with him, as did his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, and Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao.
Nine attendants including Ma Yungao, Tang Jinbao, and Zhu Zhaoyuan died with him, as did his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, and Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao.
s0137 names 馬雲皋; 雲皋 romanizes as Yungao, so Yungiao is a typographical error. The proposed replacement corrects only that personal name.
Ben's banner troops had already taken Sangui's bribes and scattered in disorder, refusing orders.
Benshen's banner troops had already taken Sangui's bribes and scattered in disorder, refusing orders.
In context after 本深不之顧, 本標兵 means Benshen's own command troops, not a personal name Ben. The proposed literal correctly attributes the bribed, disorderly banner troops to Benshen.

Sangui asked that Wenkun also hold the Yunnan governorship, ordered all troops of the governor-general's command to Yunnan under his direction, and tried to buy him off, hoping to turn him to his cause.

Sangui asked that the Yunnan governor also hold the governor-general's seal, ordered all troops of the governor-general's command to Yunnan under his direction, and tried to buy them off with profit, hoping to turn them to his cause.

s0025 has 以雲南巡撫兼督篆: Sangui asked that the Yunnan governor hold the governor-general's seal, not that Wenkun take the Yunnan post. 而以利啗之 has the 督標兵 as object, so the inducement targets the troops, not Wenkun. The proposed wording restores both points.

Southern Pacification General Aisin Gioro Shushuo was stationed at Ganzhou. Honglie wrote secretly that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Wu Youde, still remembered the dynasty's favor and that Yanling could be won back.

Southern Pacification General Aisin Gioro Shushuo was stationed at Ganzhou. Honglie wrote secretly that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Kong Youde, still remembered the dynasty's favor and that Yanling could be won back.
s0159 names 延齡妻孔四貞，定南王有德女: the father is Kong Youde (孔有德), whose surname matches the daughter's 孔. Wu Youde invents the wrong surname; Kong Youde is the correct restoration.

Southern Pacification General Aisin Gioro Shushuo was at Ganzhou; Honglie secretly wrote that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Wu Youde, had not forgotten the state's grace and Yanling could be won over.

Southern Pacification General Aisin Gioro Shushuo was at Ganzhou; Honglie secretly wrote that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Kong Youde, had not forgotten the state's grace and Yanling could be won over.
Same kinship line as the idiomatic field: 定南王有德 is Kong Youde, father of Kong Sizhen. Replacing Wu with Kong corrects the invented surname without other changes.
Honglie raised his own army and broke with Mangyitu. Isolated, he was finally undone by Chengyin.
Honglie raised a separate force of his own and then lost contact with Mangyitu. Isolated, he was finally trapped by Chengyin.

異軍特起 is rising as a separate force; 與莽依圖相失 is losing contact/becoming separated, not a deliberate break; 困於承廕 is being trapped by Chengyin. The original 'broke with' and 'undone by' misread those verbs; the proposal restores them.
